thread.title_full: LBJ takes on Flour Bluff in Week 2 test - NewsBreak

author: Cameron Wilhorn
title: LBJ takes on Flour Bluff in Week 2 test - NewsBreak
text:
By Cameron Wilhorn ,
10 hours ago LBJ captains Vicente Robles, Diego Estevis, Leo Mireles IV and Aiden De Leon against the LBJ Wolves on August 27, 2026, at Shirley Field. (Billy Woods/Laredo Morning Times) This offseason, the LBJ Wolves knew they needed to change how they approached their pre-district slate.
"We talked about if we wanted to contend for the district title and be up there with the teams in our district, we needed tougher opponents," Wolves head coach Leo Mireles said. "We knew that we could have our work cut out for ourselves, but what other way would you want it?"
More Information
LBJ (1-0)
Week 1: Aug. 27 @ Nixon (W, 40-21)
Week 2: Sept. 4 @ Flour Bluff, 7:30 p.m.
Week 3: Sept. 10 @ Winn, 7 p.m.
Week 4: Sept. 18 @ Southwest Legacy, 7:30 p.m.
Week 5: Sept. 26 vs. Del Rio, 7 p.m., SAC
Week 6: BYE
Week 7: Oct. 9 @ United, 7:30 p.m., SAC
Week 8: Oct. 15 vs. Eagle Pass, 7 p.m., SAC
Week 9: Oct. 23 @ Southwest, 8:15 p.m.
Week 10: Oct. 30 @ Alexander, 7:30 p.m., SAC
Week 11: Nov. 5 vs. United South, 7:30 p.m., SAC
A Week 2 matchup at Flour Bluff fits the mold of a tough opponent. The Hornets reached the area round of the 5A-1 playoffs last season and have won eight or more games in each of the last nine seasons. While the two teams have not met since 2009, Flour Bluff is 4-0 against the Wolves all-time. Flour Bluff did, however, lose its season opener to Corpus Christi Miller 46-41.
The matchup between LBJ and Flour Bluff is set for 7:30 p.m. Sept. 4 at Flour Bluff.
"Flour Bluff is a great playoff team. They have great tradition and great culture there," Mireles said. "(This year) they throw the ball a lot more. Their nickname of the swarm, they live up to the hype. Their defense is very fast and they get to the ball and they throw the ball around pretty good."
The Hornets played two quarterbacks during their season opener, with sophomore Michael Lawrence pacing the team with 261 passing yards and three touchdowns. But Flour Bluff's biggest offensive threats come elsewhere. They return senior pass-catcher Ransom Watson, who had 920 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns as a hybrid wide receiver and tight end last season. Tailback Samuel Smith, who rushed for 1,137 yards and 24 touchdowns, anchors the Hornets' run game. Watson and Smith both topped 160 yards from scrimmage in the Hornets' opener.
Keeping pace with Flour Bluff's potent offense is among Mireles' keys to success, but after scoring 40 points in a season-opening win against Nixon, the Wolves' offense looks to be in good form. On defense, LBJ has already seen some of its new varsity players respond well in their first test.
"We had a lot of guys that hadn't had a varsity game under their belt and they jumped into those new roles," Mireles said. "I thought those young cats did well, stepping into their new role as starters on varsity ... on the defensive side, we had our dudes that helped those younger kids out."
That first test helped LBJ's younger players settle into their roles, but Flour Bluff will provide a much stiffer challenge in Week 2. And that's exactly the type of game Mireles wanted on the schedule.
"We figured that these were the games that we wanted to play to get us ready for the playoffs," Mireles said.
